utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. I'm very sorry to say that Judge Vassylenko won't be able to join us this afternoon, so the remaining Judges decided to proceed without him in accordance with the Rule 15(B). Before we have the witness, are there any matters the parties would like to raise? Yes. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Obviously we're a little disappointed that Judge Vassylenko can't be here, but we do understand. The one matter that I did want to bring up was with respect to not this witness, but the following witness. I understand he has high blood pressure or something of that sort. Don't we all? And as I understand it that the Trial Chamber has made a decision that granting his wish to appear via videolink instead of here in person. First, let me just express my disappointment, not that it's worth a whole lot these days, but nonetheless I'm disappointed. Secondly, I think the doctor's paper is worth about 25 to 50 euros, which is what it would cost in Bosnia to purchase such a document from a doctor saying that he cannot travel. Third, the gentleman was able to travel and meet with the Prosecution not too long ago, so obviously when it's to his convenience, he can make it here. Fourth, because of the enormous amount of material that we wanted to go through and because the witness may very well not be declared a hostile witness on direct examination and because of the nature of the material, not to mention that we also recently received some additional material from the Prosecution with respect to what this witness had provided them as late -- or as early, I should say, 2002 through his lawyer, I am unwilling to relinquish I should say my position, my earlier position, of insisting that the gentleman appear here in court, recognising of course that the ultimate decision is with the Trial Chamber. But, you know, sometimes one has to make a decision; I've made my decision. And of course if the Trial Chamber feels there's no other way, then the Trial Chamber can decide on its own to drop this witness as a result of the counsel's unwillingness to entertain another form of this gentleman testifying. Now, having said that, it's our understanding that this particular witness has entered into some sort of an agreement with the Jokic Defence team, where they are willing to allow this gentleman to appear viva voce for this limited purpose of him saying on this particular day what he saw and what he heard. I don't want to go into the particulars, but nonetheless it would appear that this gentleman would be called as a Defence witness in the Jokic team, in which case I would be entitled then to cross-examine the gentleman. And in light of the logistics and in light of the time frame that we have, and so as not to disturb anything, what we would be doing is I would be asking for leave from the Trial Chamber to appear at the location where the gentleman would be sitting at testifying, so at least I could confront him eye to eye as I cross-examine him and give him documents. So in other words if he is going to be testifying via videolink, I would asking that I am present at that location. And of course everybody here can watch me from afar. So that would be my decision, Your Honour. Now, in light of that, we heard a message late Friday. So it was very difficult for us to make any other adjustments, though I have tried to make some adjustments to get some other witnesses. We will have a witness for Friday. This witness that we're about to hear will go into tomorrow, I would suspect, easily. I have lots of documents. So there is a likelihood that we will have a day free, that is around Thursday, because I don't know if I can get anybody else. I have been working on that all morning. So in any event, I just wanted to bring the Court up to speed on that, and of course again reiterate my deep -- I don't want to say dissatisfaction, but disappointment I would say with the Court's decision to allow this gentleman through this piece of paper to suggest that he cannot travel. But that's all I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any comments from the Prosecution's side?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is the first I hear of any of this. We were getting prepared to cross-examine (Redacted), so I take it he's -- none of this is going to happen this week, I imagine, given that there's a lot of logistics involved in such things. I would prefer to have a live witness as well, but do I understand he is coming live for the Jokic -- no. Okay. Well, in any event I don't really think the Prosecution is involved in this, though I would prefer to have a witness live as well. And -- but I have no knowledge or anything about his health, though he was here and looked pretty healthy when I saw him a while back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. I believe that the Trial Chamber has done it's utmost the most to try to ask this witness to come here, and even at the end of last week the chief of the witness and victim's protection unit got in touch with this witness and tried to persuade him to come here. But I'm very sorry to say that the effort has got no result. So I believe at this moment the most feasible way to hear this witness is to have the videolink or we just simply drop it off. And I'm not quite sure whether Mr. Karnavas could be on the spot during the videolink sessions. At least it's something new with me since I came to this Tribunal for four years already. But any innovative suggestions are worthy for consideration, and certainly we'll consider this suggestion and to see whether it's feasible or not. And this is also my first time to hear that this witness will testify in the Jokic case. I believe when we have more than one accused in one case, the Defence counsels are encouraged to have a combined witness, which means we don't have to call this witness twice for the different accused. So I hope after Court the parties will consult with each other on this matter and to see whether we have done -- we have to do it at this stage by the videolink or wait until the later stage, if there is a possibility for him to appear live. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, again, I'm not a medical doctor, but I would hope that the Court would reconsider, just because the person has -- one, he is reluctant to come here. I understand that. Who wants to be here as a witness? Number two, we have the power of subpoena. Number three, I think a witness simply getting a piece of paper, saying I have high blood pressure and that being an excuse for not coming over here, that to me is a way of getting around the system, and I think it sends perhaps the wrong message. Also, what if the man has to be indicted at some point, can he show this piece of paper and say, "Well, I guess he can't come and be a guest at the UN Detention Centre because he's got high blood pressure." I don't think there's sufficient grounds for this gentleman not getting on a plane and coming here, especially when he predicted this illness when I broached him the first time. He predicted he was going to be ill, so I guess he's clairvoyant as well. With respect to the joint witnesses, Mr. Stojanovic wasn't here at the time but Mr. Lukic was here at the Status Conference when we began the Defence -- prior to the beginning of the Defence case where this issue of videolink had come up and Mr. Lukic had represented to the Trial Chamber that they were going to be questioning (Redacted) on a very limited nature. Of course we anticipated that that would be coming in through the cross-examination so he wouldn't called twice. From a tactical standpoint, since I'm going to have him by videolink, as it would appear, against my wishes, might I add, I don't want to be conducting a direct examination of a witness who potentially might be hostile, not knowing whether the Trial Chamber will grant me that status of the witness being hostile, number one, so I have to control a very difficult witness on direct examination where I don't have the power of using closed-ended questions; that's number one. Number two, we have a lot of documents, so I don't know how I can physically manage to confront the witness with documents because I'm dealing with a lawyer; Mr. Vasic is a lawyer. So he's not just any kind of a witness, so that's the other thing. As far as we being present, as far as I understand it, recently there was a hearing. It got aborted at the last minute - it wasn't completely held - of a case in Rwanda where the lawyers travelled to The Hague - the witness was going to be testifying by videolink from The Hague to cross-examine the witness, where the witness would be -- for a case in Rwanda. So based on that, I thought the possibilities exist, though I don't really understand the whole notion of videolink myself. I'm not -- never done this before. But I assume that it can't be that difficult having two cameras. So since the Court, it would appear, has made a decision to have this guy testify videolink, and since I see him as a potentially dangerous witness where I need an enormous amount of control and there's going to be an enormous amount of confrontation, not in the physical sense, but in the spirit of debating, I would prefer having him for cross-examination. And because of the logistics, because of the logistics, involved, if the Jokic team were to call him as their witness, then I would be afforded my right to cross-examination. So from a tactical standpoint it makes more sense for me to have him on cross-examination than on direct examination at this stage; that's number one. And number two, I would be asking for leave to go into Bosnia, wherever the videolink is, and it may cause some disruption in the Court's calendar. Whereas if it's done during the Jokic Defence, I could arrange that ahead of time, so there's no delay on the part of me being there, I can arrange that. I don't know if I'm making a lot of sense, but in essence I've thought about this somewhat. But frankly, we could put him on the plane tomorrow, and he could be here and I think that solves everything. I'll be soft on him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think your statement is registered in the transcript. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic -- by the way, before I give the floor to Mr. Stojanovic, could I know whether this witness is a protected witness or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The one you mentioned just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As far as I understand it, he's not a protected witness. This gentleman has been contacting the Prosecution, he's been talking. All I know is he is a witness who doesn't want to come here and testify and has made it abundantly clear that he does not wish to come here at all, under any circumstances. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go into private session just for a second, just out of an abundance of caution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 25 (Redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Judge Argibay. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could have the assistance of the usher here for one second. Let me show you what has been marked for identification as Exhibit D187/1. Could you please look at it and see -- tell us if that is your name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Now, sir, could you please tell us whether you were a member of the Bratunac Brigade on July 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what your military educational background is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I completed military secondary school and military academy, major course artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How many years of education do you actually have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: That's eight years of education, military education.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And currently where are you serving?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, should we go to private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I thought we were in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll just have those places redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's all right. We'll go to private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I assumed that we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please -- I want to focus your attention to the period surrounding the fall of Srebrenica, and I'm going to give you two dates as reference points, one being July 6th, 1995, the day when the activities commenced, and July 11th, 1995, the day when we know Srebrenica fell. Could you please tell us prior to whether you, in your position, had been given any particular instructions concerning the events that were about to ensue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the positions where the men were at, how long had they been at those actual positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: They had been at these positions for a number of years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, in light of the activities that were about to occur, were you and your men given any tasks to move your positions, advance forward, and perhaps capture any enemy territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No, we weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very briefly, if you could tell us, from July 6th to July 11th, in light of your position, do you recall what activities occurred concerning your position and your men.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: We had information -- intelligence information at the time, much before the 6th of July indicating that the enemy was planning to attack our positions and to carry out a breakthrough towards Tuzla. For that purpose, the combat readiness was raised at a very high level, and that is how we understood this task at hand. And we took it very seriously and acted accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. First of all, may I ask you to explain to us, when you say "combat readiness," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: That means that any leave of soldiers from the lines were banned. That also means that we had to capture a forward command post. That also means to carry out more frequent supervision of the condition of units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: And some other activities, for instance, engineering works on fortifications, organisation of firing position systems, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, the translation here says that you had to "capture a forward command post." Did I hear you right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: That activity was often undertaken in order to be more successful in commanding. These forward command posts were usually within the combat disposition, and that is at the very front line in most cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So are you -- well, I just want to make sure I understand you correctly. Are you trying to capture a forward command post in front of the enemy, or are you trying to establish a command post, a forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No, that was my command post within the defence area of my battalion. So that was behind -- directly behind my lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you have, incidentally, a zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No. According to the rules that were in force and that we observed, a battalion has its own area of defence, not a zone of responsibility. I don't even know this term, "zone of responsibility."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, this area of defence, could you please describe it to us. What are we talking about, so we understand, we who are not in the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: An area of defence is a piece of land where the battalion is deployed for the purpose of defence. According to combat rules, a battalion should have four forward lines, a company forward and a company behind. There are some other elements of combat disposition, a command post, an anti-armour group, a unit for anti-aircraft defence, et cetera. But the main thing is that if we were to follow these rules, the battalion should have a company on the second line on fortified positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you have all of that at that time? Did you have a full --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Because we had too few soldiers and a large area that we were supposed to defend.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you have a line behind you, a second echelon line of defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, if you recall from the rules, what the length and width would be of an area of defence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: An area of defence for a battalion is from 3 to 5 kilometres, that is the area the battalion should cover on the first line. And in depth it should go from 2 to 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, going back to the events surrounding Srebrenica, from July 6th to July 11th, did you advance your positions at any point in time to capture any land?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to go day by day, and if any activity occurred, stop me and we'll talk about it. On the 6th do you know whether your soldiers were involved in any activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No, they were not, apart from those defence activities we were charged with, we were supposed to carry out a so-called decisive fatal defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this decisive defence, could you please explain to us what that term means, what does it entail?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: To put it in the simplest terms, that means the enemy under no circumstances must be allowed to cross over our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It was estimated that by threatening or even crossing an area of defence, the enemy could achieve great success in making advances into our territory. And because it is believed that the area of defence is of great importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the 7th of July, do you recall whether there was any battle activity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: During those days, we were faced with frequent provocations by the enemy, meaning that the enemy was firing at our positions from different positions and different areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And was there a response to this, to these acts of provocation or firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: In certain cases, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know whether you were firing at soldiers, whether you were firing at particularly -- at artillery equipment? What exactly were the targets that you were firing at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: We fired exclusively at enemy targets, those targets which were opening fire at us. As far as artillery is concerned, I didn't have much and I couldn't use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, what about the -- well, you said you didn't have much and you couldn't use it. Why couldn't you use it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Well, first of all, our combat sets and ammunition were incomplete. Ammunition was very short and we had to save it because we were expecting to be attacked by a brigade. That was something that we expected based on the intelligence we received.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you say that you would be attacked by a brigade. Are we speaking about the Muslim soldiers that were within Srebrenica, or are you speaking of some other brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I mean primarily members of the 28th Division of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, what about the 8th of July? Was there any action on that particular day, other than -- we've been talking about the sporadic, occasional acts of provocation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Not unlike what happened in the previous days, there were provocations but there were no shifts of units or lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what about on the 8th of July -- 7th, 8th, or 9th of July? Anything happen on that day, the 9th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: On that day, I tried to execute a demonstrative attack, more for the purpose of forced reconnaissance, of scouting of enemy positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to go step by step on this so we all understand what this term means, "demonstrative attack," and of course the purpose of forced reconnaissance. First of all, what's a demonstrative attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Well, that is an attack which is not aimed at completely capturing enemy positions. In essence, as I emphasised, it boiled down to an attempt of forcible or forced reconnaissance, aimed at establishing where the enemy was from a certain safe distance, at opening fire against those positions, finding safe cover, and observing and noting the firing positions of the enemy. So basically, it was reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what was the purpose for all of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The purpose was to gain some knowledge as to the whereabouts of the enemy, whether there were any shifts in hostile positions, what the intention of the enemy were, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what was the result of this demonstrative attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Well, unfortunately when we were moving, the commander of the scouting platoon stepped on a mine and was killed. And at the same time, his deputy was seriously wounded. As a result, we just went back to our initial positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. In this demonstrative attack, just so we are clear, did you actually capture any enemy territory? Did you go beyond the lines that you had been holding that was part of your area of defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: We did not capture anything. We did move ahead of our lines for about 100 metres maybe, 200, 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: During this demonstrative attack, do you know whether any enemy soldiers were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I know none were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I know because at the time I was at the observation post, the fog was very thick and the only sound that could be heard was this fatal explosion, fatal for my commander. And then, when I contacted that unit, I gave them orders to go back to their initial position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Just a couple of last questions on this topic. Were you ordered to carry out this demonstrative attack, or was this part of your own initiative, in light of your position at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I was given orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who gave you those orders and how were they received.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I got that order from the brigade commander, and it was brought to me by the chief of staff in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you say it was brought to you in person, so was this a written order or a verbal order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It was a written order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did the chief of staff remain there while you carried out this demonstrative attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did he participate in this event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: He participated in the sense that he followed the developments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course we're talking about Mr. Pajic. Right? Major Pajic, Novica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, this was on the 9th of July. Could you please tell us what happened, if anything, on the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: On the 10th of July, we attended the funeral of the commander who had been killed. I went briefly to that funeral. The rites were relatively short. After that, I went back to my unit. There were no major developments at that time that concerned us and our defence line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you receive any orders on that particular day to carry out any activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: July 11th, 1995, that would be the day that Srebrenica fell. Do you recall whether on that particular day you and your men did anything unusual?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No, nothing unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you receive any particular orders on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No, apart from the order to follow the situation in the territory ahead of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you -- did you or any of your men, to your knowledge, go into Srebrenica on that day, that would be the 11th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you or any of your men go to Potocari on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, before we move on to July 12th, which would be the day after Srebrenica fell, could you please tell us whether from the 6th of July to the 11th of July, whether any upper-echelon, higher-echelon, officers from the Main Staff or the corps came to your positions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the 12th of July, could you please tell us whether you received any particular orders on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, I received an order to occupy the territory of the Cizmici village and to establish a link with a neighbouring 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. That's it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And -- now, we're going to go through the map at some point, but first I just want to get the narration now. If you could just please tell us, if you recall, what the distance would be of this movement of troops.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It's not such a great distance as the crow flies, but the terrain we had to cross was very inaccessible, and there were the minefields. The minefields were obviously ahead of us and we had to move slowly that day, with a great deal of caution. And having set out somewhere in the afternoon, we managed to take hold of that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, during that particular day, did you come across any prisoners, you or the soldiers, the units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you come across, if you recall, any dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you come across any abandoned weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Not large-calibre weapons. Maybe a soldier or two came across an abandoned rifle or something like that, but there were no cannons or anything like that. I don't remember seeing any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. On that particular day, do you recall whether you observed enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you observe a column of Muslims coming from Srebrenica, for instance, heading in a particular direction? Did you notice that? Now, we're talking about the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Not on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just to be on the safe side, had you noticed, had you noticed, prior to July 12th, any enemy forces on the move?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we're going to go step by step. When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: That was in the evening of the 10th, that is, in the early evening hours on the 10th of July. And on the 11th, throughout the day, you could see that column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us how far this column was from you, what the distance would be.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: At least 5, 6, maybe more, kilometres, as the crow flies, distance from the first, foremost, defence line, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you describe to us the terrain. What was the terrain like that separated you and your men and the column that you had observed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The terrain was rather rough, inaccessible, criss-crossed in various ways by brooks and some other natural features, obstacles such as forest, woods, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In light of this terrain, could you please tell us how you were able to observe this column, especially from the distance that you've indicated to us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: My forward command post was on top of a dominant feature, from which one could observe using sights, optical instruments, and the naked eye even, that in the area around Jaglic there was a moving column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it you had optical instruments like binoculars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes, some binoculars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, first of all, did you at any point in time attack this column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you ever ordered to attack this column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ever advance to try to capture this column or members of this column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you inform anyone that you had seen, observed, this column of men going in a particular direction, which I am sure, in light of your background and experience of the terrain, knew fairly well where they were heading toward?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: We were reporting to the duty officer of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How would you or how did you report to the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: By communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But you got to tell us what those communication means were, because we weren't there. So what did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: We had telephones and field radio devices, RUP-12 and similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you have a Motorola with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At this point in time when you saw this column and you told us it was the night of the 10th and then on the 11th, did you at any point in time, to the best of your recollection, call your commander, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, to inform him of what you had seen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is there a particular reason why you didn't call your commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: During those days, our official communication was very poor. My communications were mainly directed towards the duty officer of the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it once you pass on a message, one might expect that the duty officer would do something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just so I'm not leading you and draw an objection, what might that be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I expected him to inform officers in charge, the brigade commander, and other higher-ranking officers --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: -- for the purpose of having an insight into the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But in light of what you had seen, would it not also make sense for you to contact someone like the head of intelligence and security of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Because, and that is what the rules say, I was to communicate directly only with the commander or perhaps his deputy because I was directly subordinated to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, in light of the information that you had passed on, did you at any point in time receive any orders as to what if anything, or what if any actions you should take with respect to the column that you had seen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: We received no orders whatsoever regarding the column, in terms of doing anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you told us that on the 12th you had moved your positions, and I believe we had finished with the 12th. So now let's move on to the 13th. Could you please tell us what, if anything, you and your men did on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: My activities were focused, on the 13th of July, on linking up with the 2nd Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you say "linking up," what are we talking about? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: That means that we had first to spot where their position was, that they see us as well; that we coordinate fire, if necessary, for us to defend ourselves; to exchange information, if there was any; and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And why was that necessary, the link-up? You told us what it is, now tell us why. Why would that be important, if it is? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It is important because between my battalion and the 2nd Battalion, there was a gap of space that under such circumstances the enemy might have made use of in terms of inflicting losses on our forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you link up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall about when? What day? What time? What place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I personally went with some officers, and we went to the village of Pale. That is where I met the commander. I think it was the 5th Company of the 2nd Infantry Battalion. And I remember that on that particular day, we discussed the defence system established by the enemy facing us, because in that particular area they had some fortified features. And we managed to observe an anti-aircraft gun positioned there, enemy gun, and I think there was also an anti-aircraft machine-gun. That was basically what we discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what time of day would this have been?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: That was on the morning of the 13th when I managed to meet them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on that day do you know whether you and the others, the ones that you had linked up with, whether you were engaged in any activities with the enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: On that day we didn't see any enemy forces, either individuals or any major units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you see any dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you come across any abandoned weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Except this four-barrel gun, anti-aircraft gun that I mentioned earlier, and an anti-aircraft machine-gun, we didn't find any other weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in getting to this position on the 13th, as you've indicated to link-up, having moved your positions on the 12th through the 13th, did you -- were you searching the terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Well, you cannot say exactly that we did that, but we did try to find out what was happening in front of us, behind us, to the extent possible under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, maybe you can help us out here a little bit. First of all, let's try to figure out what is the manner in which one would go about searching the terrain. Could you please describe that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Well, the searching of terrain is a preventive scouring action taken with the aim of having control over a territory in terms of finding out whether there are any so-called remaining parts left behind by the enemy or any infiltrated sabotage groups or military equipment or weapons and some other minor tasks or purposes that this whole operation is undertaken for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, that's a nice definition, but concretely could you tell me how would this be carried out? We know the purpose, now tell me how.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It is carried out by -- from a particular position, depending on the problems that we anticipate to face, we head off from the so-called blockade line in a combat disposition of troops and scour the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, again, does that mean that the soldiers are walking one behind another in a column, or are they spread out and are they moving in a spread position? Which of the two concretely? Remember, we're are not soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes. Soldiers move in a combat disposition, which means that they are 6 to 8 or 10 metres apart from each other or from one another, that they have a visible contact between one another. And in the process, they undertake all measures against any possible surprises.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now that we know how one would go about searching the terrain, concretely tell us how you and the men moved on the 12th to the 13th when you went and you linked up with the 2nd Battalion. In what manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Most often we moved in columns that are secured; in combat terms, they had flank security, front security, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is there a particular reason why you moved mostly in columns versus spreading out in a combat disposition format?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes. The reason is mostly difficult terrain that we had the task of moving across. Also, this area contained minefields that we didn't know the location of, and that is what put restrictions on our movement along certain roads, like village roads and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the 13th after linking up, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: On the 13th, I went to my command post in Cizmici, and that took place in the early evening hours. Before that, I visited part of the units in order to see how the situation was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the 14th, could you please tell us what, if anything, you and the men did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: On the 14th, we didn't move anywhere. On the 14th, I also visited my troops because I wanted to organise the so-called firing system in order to prevent any possible surprises from taking place. I also wanted to see how the situation in the battalion was, where the companies and platoons were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I believe, I believe, that this may be time for the break. And if that is the case, then perhaps we can pick up with you explaining to us about why you needed to organise your firing system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We now have a break. We'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, sir, I believe we left off where you indicated that on July 14th one of the things that you wanted to do was organise your firing system. Could you please tell us what do you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It's an undertaking that is always done in order to identify specific tasks of the units on the ground to identify the axis of firing from the weapons that we have at our disposal, and if necessary to create minefields. In short, to undertake all necessary measures in order to undertake the most effective defence as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if I understand you, was part -- was the firing in relation to identifying the range of how far the weapons could fire so then you would know where to lay the mines, the land mines? Is that -- am I correct at understanding your rather technical answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes, there is a connection, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on the 14th did you do anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Nothing in particular, apart from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you move your troops in any way? Did you search any terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the 15th of July do you recall that day, and if so, could you please tell us what, if anything, you and the men did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was heavy rain on that day. And I believe that that was a very powerful limiting factor for any sort of activities that we were supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you had received any orders? I know that we have the rain and it's a limiting factor, but did you in fact receive any orders that you were required to carry out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: We had received an order to search the terrain along a specific axis, and as I understood the task was to cover the axis that we already were deployed on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you in fact search the terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: We didn't do that either on the 14th or the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you by any chance notify your commander by way of passing a message through the duty officer that you were unable to carry out the order that had been issued to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I cannot remember that specific detail, but I presume that it was clear to everyone that because of the rain we were not able to move forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the 14th or the 15th, did you or your men come across any enemy soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you come across any dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you come across any abandoned weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on that 15th, the 15th of July, is there anything else about that particular day that may be of significance for this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: One of those days, I think it was the 15th or the 16th - and I think it was the 16th - I was visited by the commander, Lieutenant Colonel Cvjetinovic. He visited me at my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Just to make sure we got it correct, you were visited by the commander and, and, Lieutenant Colonel Cvjetinovic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, that both of them came to see me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But your commander at that point in time was Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall about what time of day this would have been?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I suppose that it must have been in the afternoon. I can't tell you the exact hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall what the nature of the visit was, the purpose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: They were just inspecting the troops, they wanted to see where we were, what we were doing, because we didn't communicate too often in those days. They simply wanted to see what the situation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us approximately how long they were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Perhaps an hour. I'm not sure. I think it was for about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And during that hour or approximate one hour that they were there visiting and checking up, did you by any chance notify them of any particular problems that you might have been having at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I informed them about the situation prevailing in the unit, about the problems that I faced, because many soldiers were wandering about at that time. I also described the situation in the unit, our specific position, and some other details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know approximately how many soldiers were out wandering about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say exactly, to give you a number, but there were cases of individuals who abandoned their positions at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Please tell us where these soldiers would have gone, if you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: They most probably went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you say "home," where are we speaking about, back in Bratunac or some other location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Bratunac, most probably. In fact, my soldiers were mostly from the surrounding villages or the area of Podrinje and other villages, which means that they did not come from the urban parts. And I demanded at that time the military police to intensify their operations in case they came across such soldiers to send them immediately back to their positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the 16th did you receive any particular orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: On the 16th we started the scouring of the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And in which direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: In the direction of Lupoglava and approximately towards the village which I think is called Susnjari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, was that pursuant to an order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No. Since the order had a different instruction contained in it, which was rather unclear to me, that was exactly the reason because of these ambiguities that we continued to move from the point where we had been, that is, from the line that we were on on the 14th and the 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Incidentally, when you had brought to the attention of the military police, as I believe you indicated, that if they came across any men to send them back to the unit, do you know whether any men were in fact sent back to the unit by the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In searching the terrain - and we're going to go through the documents, the orders, and the map - but in searching the terrain, do you recall whether you came across any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Any dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Any abandoned weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Are you referring to the 16th?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No, we didn't find any.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you by any chance engage -- were you engaged, you and the others? Were you engaged by any enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us for how long did this searching operation go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Well, it lasted throughout the 16th and only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what about the 17th? What, if anything, did you do on that day if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I remember receiving an order to line up my battalion in the area of my former command post in order to execute the mission of going to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And was that carried out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us when you left for Zepa, what day, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: On the 17th of July, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was that the entire unit, the entire battalion, or were some, if you know, left behind to carry out any other orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The entire battalion went on that mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you by any chance ever receive an order to send anyone to Zvornik, to the Zvornik area during those days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I think I did. I can't remember the exact date now. But I think I was to send one platoon to the Zvornik area, but that was not done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Why was it not done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Because we had other commitments connected to our going to Zepa, and the entire unit was required to go there and join in the activities in the area of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recall what the reason was that you were asked to send a size of a platoon to go Zvornik, what the purpose ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I don't remember the reason why that was asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Concretely, were you ever asked to supply men so they could carry out executions that were ongoing in that area or any other area during those critical days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No, that was never asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you supply men to other areas, either at that time or prior to that time, to cover other areas outside the area of defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where that would have been.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: A smaller part of the forces was in the area of Trnovo, and a part was also engaged in the area of Pjenovac, towards Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to stop here before we talk about any other periods and I want to go back now and go through some documents and some maps. So first, with the assistance of the usher, I would like to show you what has been -- what has come into evidence as P406/A. And I believe we can even put one on the ELMO. First of all, do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, for the record, what is this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It is an order for active combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall ever seeing this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us in this particular document what section, if any, would relate to you and your troops, what paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The first point, "Information on the Enemy," is also relevant to us because that was important to me. But specifically related to me are points 5, "Tasks to subordinate units" is the subtitle, which emphasises that the 1st Infantry Battalion is to carry out decisive defence along its current combat positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to go step by step.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, was that carried out, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now we'll go to the next sentence, next paragraph. It talks about the use of a large-calibre weapon, a PAM anti-aircraft machine, 76 millimetres, self-propelled gun, 30-millimetre guns, and so on. Were these weapons used, sir, the one that are reflected in this exhibit under paragraph 5.1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: A 30-millimetre gun was out of order. Its brakes were broken, and it was unable to move. It was mounted on an old FAP truck, and it was practically inoperative. The self-propelled vehicle was on its position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: And there were the PAMs, the anti-aircraft machine-guns. But even there, as far as the self-propelled vehicle is concerned, I had problems with fuel. So it was practically unusable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we know that one had some problems, the other one is practically unusable. Did you in fact use these large-calibre weapons, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I think we used them on the 12th of July when advancing towards the area of Cizmici village for the purpose of combat support to our activities; intermittently and very briefly we used them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, were they directed towards enemy forces, visible enemy forces, on that day, the 12th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: On that day we did not observe the enemy, but we knew where the enemy positions were. We could see their trenches and we assumed that their points of resistance were there. For instance, the trig point 413 frequently opened fire at me, machine-gun fire, and we targeted it most frequently. It was located in the woods but on a dominant feature facing us. And our fire was mostly directed at them, in order to secure the movement of our columns, which were required on the 12th to take hold of Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But on that day, on that particular day, were you fired upon? You said that you were frequently fired upon from I believe it was trig point 413, but concretely on July 12th do you recall whether you were fired upon before you fired at those observation posts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I cannot now precisely recall that detail, but it's quite possible that even that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we go to the next paragraph. It says: "Have the reconnaissance platoon ready to repel a possible enemy attack." Did you, sir, have a reconnaissance platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you -- did it have a particular name, some insignia that it would be recognisable, like a red beret or something that would have them set off from the rest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who were these members of this reconnaissance platoon? Where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: They were part of the battalion, and they had been withdrawn from the defence lines so as to give me some minimal backup.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us about how many were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: About 20, 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were they specialised, trained? You know, when we hear reconnaissance, we think of special forces. Were these the sort of folks that we're talking about, highly trained, highly disciplined, highly motivated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, it then goes on to say --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. It then goes on to say that it is "responsible for the link-up with the 4th Battalion." I take it that's what it says. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you link up with the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: We did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And do you recall whether this linkage occurred prior to or during those critical days, the 6th through the 11th, or was it at some other point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- then it says that it will "support the Bratunac artillery group from current positions according to the plan and requests." First of all, who are or what is this Bratunac artillery group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Those were 76-millimetre guns, as far as I know. Some 105-millimetre Howitzers, and I believe there were also some 122-millimetre guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And did you provide any support for them? Were there any requests?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Then it says I believe that your forward command post is supposed to be in this Vresinje sector. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, is that where you set it up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, could you please tell us when was it that you first saw this particular order.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: This order was brought to me by the chief of staff in person when he came to my unit on the 6th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Prior to the 6th of July, were you aware, were you aware, that you would be receiving such an order, an order that would require you to carry out these activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall whether you had attended any meetings prior to the 6th of July that -- where you would have been informed of any activities that were about to commence regarding Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, I want to show you another document, what has been marked, I believe, for identification purposes as D185. Could you please look at that, sir. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And we may not wish to show the signature, the name on that document, but -- all right. And what do you recognise it to be, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It is a perfectly regular request for resupply of equipment and materiel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in looking at this one would suspect that the material that is being requested is in light of perhaps activities that are about to commence. Would I be correct in reaching that conclusion or making that assumption?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Because first of all I was not even aware of the activities that followed immediately, not at the time, and in view of the current supplies of ammunition and fuel, tractor fuel, that we had in our unit, this is a quite usual request, a quite normal communication, with the logistical unit under the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, concretely, sir, can you be a little more specific? I mean, let's look at, for instance, diesel. Here you're asking for 40 litres.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes. These are extremely low quantities that I was requesting. If you know that the general situation with fuel in our brigade had always been bad, fuel was always a problem. With this kind of fuel, you can cross 10 kilometres, perhaps, with certain vehicles. And this request emphasises the reason why we were requesting replenishment for the medical unit, for instance. Even under circumstances where there is no fighting, troops can get hurt. And it is quite normal that the medical unit should have fuel to transport the wounded. I mentioned a moment ago that my self-propelled gun was out of fuel, and that is confirmed in this request. In order to have a mobile self-propelled gun in case of an attack, I needed fuel. All that was on my mind at the time. I was expecting at the time an attack from a brigade-sized enemy unit, and I needed this equipment and materiel in order to be able to defend my area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So it's your explanation today, if I can just encapsulate it is that this request --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's totally unnecessary for Mr. Karnavas to put his own interpretation on the explanation. We've heard it. We've all heard the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to show you another document. This has come in. This is marked D149. You may wish to keep D185 there just in case we may need to make reference to it. Perhaps it may be necessary; perhaps not. If I could show you this document; it's dated July 3rd, 1995. You do know Mr. Trisic, do you not, the assistant commander for logistics?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is there anything in this document where he's making a request, an urgent request, to the Drina Corps that might be relevant to your request that you made on 4 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It could be relevant. It says explicitly here that he is urgently requesting certain equipment and materiel. I see ammunition, fuel, motor vehicles, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well -- but how can he -- his is dated July 3rd. Yours is dated July 4th. How is it that he can forecast what your needs might be?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's a totally inappropriate question. It's speculative. I don't see how the witness can answer that. It should have been a question put to Mr. Trisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, first of all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: A question can be inappropriate without being totally inappropriate. It's either inappropriate or it's not, but be that as it may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But you're asking this witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's saying that July 3rd might be relevant. The two documents may be related. He's made a request to Trisic who is responsible for these matters. I'm asking him to exercise, you know, his opinion based on the facts on the ground as to whether Mr. Trisic would have known what his needs would have been for him to put in such a request to the Drina Corps. I don't think it's speculative at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, first you have to know whether this witness at that time was aware of this document or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll go around it another way, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In determining what materiel you would need, what would you do or who would handle that for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: My assistant commander for logistics would deal with that on my behalf.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who would he deal with? Who would he contact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: He would deal with the assistant commander for logistics at brigade level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know if there was a procedure, if there was, when and if new supplies came in whether the different battalions were informed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And based on that information, that is, assuming that the assistant commander for logistics had informed you that new supplies had come in, what, if anything, would you or your logistics man do based on that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I would submit my request for replenishment for these particular supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. We can go on to another document. Actually, this is a series of documents; they're daily combat reports. And I'm going to start with what has come into evidence as P411. And I'm going to go through these rather quickly so you can comment on the relevant portions. Now, first of all -- do you see, I've just handed you what has been marked as P411. Do you recognise the document, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from looking at it, what do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It is a regular or daily combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you could direct our attention to any particular paragraph in this daily combat report that would be relevant to you in particular.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I cannot distinguish the date here. I cannot find it. Maybe there is a better copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you say you cannot -- which date are we talking about? The date when this document was generated? I can assure you, at least based on what we know, that this is 6 July 1995. And you may want to look at the bottom, towards the signature.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It's clear now. What is relevant to me is para 1, which mentions that the enemy had opened fire at the right flank of the 2nd Infantry Battalion and the left flank of the 1st Infantry Battalion from trig point 413 and carried out provocations along the entire defence line of the brigade, which means that the paragraph specifies the left flank of my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and if I may go back to what you stated earlier, when you indicated that there were occasions when you were fired upon, was this the same trig point, 413?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is there anything else in this particular daily combat report dated 6 July 1995 that you would like to draw our attention to that you find worthy of noting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to the fact that in my view this report was not written by the commander because this is simply not his phraseology. What you find here is the word "Turk converts," and that's not the kind of word he used. I think, therefore, that this was written by somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Anything else? All right --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go on to the next document, and this would be P412/A. In your case, it would be /B, since we're talking about the Srpski version. Again, it's maybe rather rough to read, but if you could look at it and please tell us what this is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: This is a document similar to the previous one, only with different content, another daily combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What is the date on this one, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page one can see that it's dated the 7th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you direct our attention to any particular paragraph in this daily combat report that is dated 7 July 1995 that is relevant to you and your troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It is mentioned here TT.413 again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: And it also says that enemy opened fire at our positions, just like on the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did that occur, sir? To your recollection, did the enemy open fire toward your positions on that particular day, that is 7th July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if we go into paragraph 2, it says: "Our forces returned the fire and also fired artillery at the enemy's firing positions." So, question: Is that referring to you or to your troops, that is, returning the fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Because I didn't have any artillery weapons, so my forces could only have fired from infantry weapons and return fire aiming at certain sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So from that you can conclude -- you're concluding that this would not have been you because you did not have artillery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, what sort of -- other than, you know, the regular weapons that the soldiers carried, what sort of heavy weaponry did you and your men have at that particular time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: With the exception of small arms, we also had 82-millimetre and 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, what's the difference? Can't we conclude that that's sort of in the same ballpark range of artillery, or are we talking about different strength, different impact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Well, according to our rules, this is not considered artillery, both from the point of view of range and also according to the establishment, because they are assigned to infantry battalions. This is not a separate, an independent, unit, but it's rather part of an infantry battalion. The range of these weapons is very small. And what I would like to say is that I had an extreme shortage of ammunition for these particular weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Those are the mortars we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just so I'm clear, just so I'm clear, did you fire at all any mortars on the 6th or the 7th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to -- is there anything else about this document that catches your attention that might be worthy of commenting on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: This document is pretty unclear -- I mean, the copy is very bad, so I just cannot discern what it says, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let's move on to the next document. This has come into evidence as P413. You will be looking at /B, while we look at 413/A. Would you please look at this, sir, and tell us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: This is a daily combat report dated 8th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, as with the previous two documents, can you focus our attention on any particular paragraph that might be relevant to you and your troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
