utterances.text: The point where it says that officers are either at their forward command positions or at the battalion command, and partly it is relevant in item 1 where it says that the enemy launched a diversion or a mock attack from the direction of Kosa on the right flank of my 4th Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, first of all, what is a mock attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It's an attack, the purpose of which is to engage certain enemy forces in order to divert the attention of the enemy. It's a kind of cunning move, if I may say so. So the point, the focus, of the attack is not to capture, to occupy, certain axis or a sector, but rather to create a diversion in order to focus the attention of the enemy on another axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Anything else about this particular combat report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: There is something illogical, in my view, and that is towards the end of this report where it says -- where it speaks about the conception of 130-millimetre bullets, 90-millimetre bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What's wrong with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It seems to me to be illogical that -- because, as per establishment, we didn't have this kind of ammunition, either in that period or after.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we're speaking about the first two items that are listed --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That would be on paragraph 6 of this document, which is P413. Don't worry about the P413, that's the identification number of the document itself. We're talking about bullets, 130-millimetre, and bullets 90-millimetre. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on to the next document. If you can please take a look at P415. We'll be looking at /A while you look at /B. Would you please tell us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: This is a daily combat report dated 9th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as with the previous three documents, could you please direct our attention to the appropriate paragraph that is relevant to you and your troops.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The paragraph that was relevant for us is item 5 where it says: "Injured/Wounded." This paragraph reads that during the active combat operations, my battalion suffered casualties in terms that the people named here were wounded and one of them died. And it says that he died before he was transported to the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And this is in relation to what you had told us earlier about the activities that you had carried out on 9th -- 9 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, again if we could look at the paragraph number 6, "Consumption," that section. Again, is there anything there that seems illogical in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes, there is. Bullet 100-millimetres, it could only be a bullet for an anti-armour gun, and it can also be for a T-55 tank. We also didn't have this kind of weapons. Next, shells, 90-millimetre Panzer and 90-millimetre TF, were also something we didn't need because we didn't have that kind of weapons. I also failed to mention bullets 30/2, which are used by anti-aircraft guns known as Praga. We also didn't have such weapons. In other words, I don't understand why this report contains consumption of the weapons that we actually didn't have, as per establishment in our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if you could refresh our memory again before we go into any more documents. Again, what was your specialised training in the military, in what area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: My specialty is artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So I take it in light of that background you would know about these sorts of matters that we're speaking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then lastly if we could go up the page to paragraph 2, is there anything in this particular paragraph which would give us an impression as to your whereabouts on this particular day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It says here the chief of staff was in the area of responsibility, which I think is a wrong term because a battalion doesn't have an area of responsibility, at least I don't know of any such case. The same applies to the brigade. So it says the chief of staff is, as I understand it, in the area which is covered by my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, let's go on to the next document, P416. And again, you'll be looking at 416/B, while we look at 416/A. Could you please tell us what this document is, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: This is a daily combat report dated 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as with the previous daily reports that we've looked at, could you please focus our attention to the appropriate paragraph that is pertinent to you and your troops.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Item 1 which says that "enemy carried out combat activities all along the brigade defence line" is the one pertaining to my unit. And probably this implies that the enemy had committed acts of provocations, as they had done before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Also where it says that the chief of staff is in the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Was he at that point in time, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And was he doing anything in particular during those days while he was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: He was surveying the situation in the battalion, how ready we were for defence in the defence area that we covered. He was issuing certain directives and guidelines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you. Now, I think we'll go on to another document. And this is what has been marked and entered into exhibit as D131/1. If you could look at that. Now, recognising that you did not generate this document, that is a document that was prepared or at least signed by Trisic, the assistant commander for logistics on 12 July 1995, could you please tell us whether there are any items listed from 1 to 17 that are relevant to your unit or your troops.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: This deals with the consumption of materiel and equipment, and it has been compiled in the form of a report submitted by the assistant commander for logistics for this specific period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recognise any items on this list that would have been dispensed to you or your men during this period, that is, from the 10th to the 12th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I cannot say that among these 35-odd thousand bullets were the bullets fired by some of my soldiers from their positions. But if you allow me, I would like to draw your attention to what specifically says this -- the previous reports referred to when it comes to the consumption of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Item 6, "bullet 30 millimetres". This confirms that we are talking about gun or cannon 30/2 known as Praga. Item 7 is not quite clear in the copy that I have in front of me. Then item number 12, "bullet 90 millimetres" which refers to M36 self-propelled gun, and it says specifically so here. This is also one of the weapons that we didn't have, as per establishment. Next item, "bullet 100 millimetres" confirms that this refers to a tank, because T stands for a tank, and the number is 55. Likewise, we didn't have such weapons in our unit. Next one, "bullet 105 Howitzer," we did have those, however "bullet 122 millimetres" also indicates it's used for Howitzers, not guns, but this is the type of Howitzers that we didn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You told us earlier that "bullet 30 millimetres" that says cannon 30/2, you did not have the weapon for the consumption of those bullets. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes, we didn't have this kind of weapon known as Praga.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just for your information item 7 says: "Bullet 30 millimetres, cannon with MiG. Expansion unknown."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: With MiG. That's a cannon with -- that is an explanation for an airplane, but it's not clear to me either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Just drawing your attention lastly to 16. On your -- in light of your experience with this particular brigade, do you feel confident in commenting on item 16 where it talks about diesel, the disbursement of 3.039 litres of diesel during this two-day period?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's a very broad question, Your Honour. We don't know what the question is. Commenting on what? In respect of what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure whether there is any vehicles in that battalion. You know, there has to be some connections with this witness, you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: (Redacted) I'm asking him in light of his knowledge and experience in being in that brigade, he would have known, as he knows about all these other items, whether this particular brigade had the sort of equipment that would have consumed 3.000 litres in a period of two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may put this question to this witness, but I am not quite sure we could get an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I'll lay some foundation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You began serving with the Bratunac Brigade about what time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: From the 1st of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So by July 12, 1995, we're talking a little bit over two years being in the Bratunac Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in light of your position, the position that you held within the brigade, and in light of having served in that brigade for a period of two years, do you feel competent enough to comment on the number of vehicles the brigade would have had at this particular time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I can say that it had a few vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in your opinion - that's all we can ask for - but in your opinion, is this figure of 3.039 litres of diesel being consumed in a period of two days, is that consistent with the number of vehicles that you knew the Bratunac Brigade had and was able to actually -- that were actually functioning and capable of consuming that amount of petrol in two days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I don't think that was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We can move on to the next document. Now, if I could show you another series of reports starting with exhibit P441/A. You will be looking at /B. If you could look at this document, sir, and please tell us what is it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It's a daily combat report dated 12th July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 12 July 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, as with the previous daily combat report, if you could assist us in focusing our attention to the relevant paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: There is something really illogical in this report in my view, and that is that there is no mention of what our units did specifically on that day. There is no mention here that together with other -- with the 2nd Infantry Battalion we carried out certain tactical shifting of troops. There is also no mention of the lines reached. Generally, my impression is that someone compiled this report in a haste, and this shows that in that period we did have certain problems, particularly in terms of coordination among our respective units and activities, in that we needed some more specific instructions as to what to do at specific times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If I could focus your attention to paragraph 2 in the English version, I don't know how it comes out in your language, but it says: "Our forces are mopping up the enclave and preventing the enemy from breaking through in the above-mentioned direction." First of all, this "mopping up," what does that mean, to mop up, if there is such a thing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It's a jargon term. This is not a regular military term. And I can't say -- can't understand specifically what the author meant by this in this particular report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You can or you cannot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Is there anything else that you find illogical or out of order in this particular daily combat report dated 12 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: What strikes me - and that even more corroborates my previous claim that somebody really wrote this in a hurry - is the statement under item 5 where it says that we will submit details of consumption of ammunition and fuel later. In the previous reports, this had always been very specifically stated; however, in this report there is no mention of that. And I don't understand the reason why.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go on to the next document, P469/B. And just for the record, we do appreciate the enormous amount of assistance from the usher, who is traversing back and forth with these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before we get to this document, Mr. President, I'm not used to the afternoon hours. Is it time or am I mistaken?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's time, but if you feel it's necessary we could continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Until you finish this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, there are some other documents that go along with this document. And so we can break at this point, because I'm afraid that it will go on for at least another 10 minutes to finish the other two documents that accompany this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll have a break and we'll resume at 10 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, sir, I believe we left off as we were about to launch into the daily combat report dated 13 July 1995. Is that correct? Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. And for the record, I'm referring to what is marked as P469. Now, in looking at this daily combat report, as you have with the previous ones, could you direct our attention to the pertinent paragraph as it relates to you and your men.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I would draw your attention to this reference that says that we are searching the terrain. In fact, we were not searching the terrain that day. The area of Milacevici and Babuljica villages was the territory ahead of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, can you account for such a mistake in this daily combat report and why would they include something that's not accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The person who wrote this, and I suppose that was the duty officer, the duty operative officer, was not in possession of specific information as to our whereabouts and our current activities. That could be an explanation, or maybe the duty officer thought that it was his duty to write this report this way as --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm objecting to that. That's totally speculative and it's a conclusion that I don't believe the witness is in a position to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I did not see this battalion the witness was belonging to was mentioned in this document. I believe that this document is talking about the whole brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could go back, Your Honour, I'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Looking at this particular document, which of the seven paragraphs that are numbered are related to your battalion specifically, if any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Well, looking at this document I suppose that para 2 is relevant. "During the search of Milacevici and Babuljica villages, our forces did not meet any resistance." It's true that we did not meet any resistance, but as to major movements of our forces, we were not actually searching the terrain. We were linking up or joining up with the 2nd Infantry Battalion. Somebody could have interpreted that as a search of the terrain, although these are two different actions, search of the terrain as opposed to joining up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Just to be on the safe side, which paragraph of the seven were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Item 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so what you're telling us is that item 1 is not accurate, at least to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we could go on to the next report. I want to show you now what has been marked as P485. We're looking at /A; you're looking at /B. Could you please look at this, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: This is a daily combat report dated the 14th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And is there any particular paragraph that you want to draw our attention to that relates specifically to your battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: In para 1, reference is made to the terrain where our forces were doing a search. And it says that no enemy forces were spotted, nor did we come across any enemy; that could be a reference to me and it probably was. On that day I did not come across or had any contact with any enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And on that particular day, were you searching the terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Is there anything else that you want to draw our attention to on this particular one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Maybe the point where it says that on the territory which our brigade was supposed to cover in an operative way, there was no danger or there was danger of enemy attack, enemy surprise attack, which is in line with what I thought, namely that we had to be ready and prevent any surprises.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And again, before I move from this document to the next, drawing your attention to paragraph 2 it talks about a particular order, does it not, with respect to searching and clearing the terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And is it your understanding, sir, that on this particular day, that is 14 July 1995, you and your men were --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's clearly leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you on this particular day, 14 July 1995, carry out any searching activities, as reflected in paragraph 2 pursuant to an order numbered 157/5?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, speaking of that order perhaps it would be an opportune time to go to that. So I would like to draw your attention to what has been marked and entered into evidence as P472. This will be the first document that we look at. Now, from the previous document that I had just shown you, if you may recall, it said that the order was numbered 4-157-5. In looking at this document, sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- would this be the order itself that the previous document, that is, Exhibit P485 shown to you, was referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you would please look at it for a second, and if you could please tell us, first of all, what is this order for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It is an order to search the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It is unclear who signed it, but I suppose it is Major General Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And to whom is it directed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: In the beginning of the document, it is indicated that it was directed towards the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, and the Skelani Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, and then in looking at this particular document without going into any great details, which of the six enumerated paragraphs concern the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The document is poorly legible, but para 2 seems to be relevant -- no, para 1, sorry, para 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and are you able to at least make out the areas that you are being asked to -- that the Bratunac Brigade is being asked to search, or would you want me to read the English translation for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: If you please, because the document is illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Under paragraph 1 it says: "The 1st Light Infantry Brigade, Bratunac Brigade, shall search the terrain of the former Srebrenica enclave up to the following line: Ravni Buljim. Excluded; Zvijezda, trig point 906." I would have practiced that, had I known I was going to be reading this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Siljato Brdo, trig point 901; Slapovici village along Zeleni Jadar river bank up to Zeleni Jadar bridge excluded." Okay. Now, I want to show you the next document, which is P483 which has come into evidence. And if you look at this. And you may want to keep -- you may want to have handy the previous document as well just there, just in case. All right. Now, do you recognise what this document is, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It is an order for terrain search.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And which of the enumerated seven paragraphs relate to your battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Para 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you compare paragraph 1 of the document that I've given you, which is dated 14 July 1995, and it's P483, with the previous document which was dated July 13, 1995, and that would be P472, the areas which you are being asked to search, do they correspond roughly, generally, in principle, with the areas which are in the order by Major General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: This is just an attempt to translate this order by Radislav Krstic into operational terms, but in the execution part there are some illogical terms. And it is not quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to show you a map, and this is D186 for identification. If you could please take a look at it, keeping the documents that you have in front of you, especially the one dated 14 July. If I could first show you this document which has been marked for identification as D187. Perhaps we can put this -- well, first you can look at it and then we'll take it from there step by step. First of all, do you recognise this map, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And are there any notations on this particular map which you recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what are those notations, in general? We're going to get into --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm wondering if, Your Honour, perhaps we can put this on the ELMO so we can follow along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. President, Mr. President, I can understand how the Prosecutor is anxious for us to get to the map; however, first, I don't want the gentleman's signature and name to be appearing on the ELMO since this is a protected witness. I wish for him first to identify the document to make sure that this is the map he has marked. And then from there we were going to go on to the specific areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have already taken some measures that anything on the ELMO will not be available on the public TV outside this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please -- we're going to put this map on that little projector; we call it ELMO here. The gentleman is going to take the map from you; he's going to put it on the ELMO. And you're going to be able to see it on the screen. If we can open up the map so we can see where your signature line is. Delicately, please. First of all, if we could please --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could gently look at this map. On this particular map, do you see your signature, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And is there a date by your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: There is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what that date is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The 15th December, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And could you please tell us -- this map has some markings. Are those your markings, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us when you made those markings.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: On that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Before the gentleman from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So -- and where was that, just so we have a record of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: At the international motel in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So these markings were made when you were giving a statement to the Prosecutors. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you can first of all -- we're going to go from the general to the specific. So first of all, please explain to us what these markings are that you've made. And the usher there is going to gently slide the map as you describe the points, the various points, on the map. So first, what are we looking at that you have marked on this particular map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: On this map I marked the defence lines primarily of my battalion, and then those of other battalions of our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you -- we're going to give you a pointer, and you're going to have to point on the map itself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do it rather delicately. If you could point to us exactly where is the 1st Battalion on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The 1st Infantry Battalion was on the line from Lomanac Brook, including that brook, then Pajici village. Trig point 405 Lemesac. Then there is an interruption in the line. The line is broken perhaps because maps existed in different editions, in different years. And they do not continue on to each other. And then follows trig point 532. And these two maps were given me separately, to mark them. So here I made an error regarding the positions overlooking Blazevici. The positions were not exactly where I drew them, but were from trig point 555, excluding trig point 555. There is an old dirt road here, and it ends here at Ilina Brdo, Ilina Hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if you could correct the map, since you indicated that these were two separate maps that are now stapled -- we Scotch-taped them together. If you could make that slight correction and do it here in open court, gently.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And perhaps for that little stretch of the terrain, we can even have you initial it so we know that you indeed made that marking. Maybe put a date on it, too. I think we're on July -- June, June 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could just go through some of the other markings briefly, just very briefly. Tell us what else you have marked on this map. We don't need to know the exact trig points, but what else does this map have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: On this map we see other markings designating the areas of defence or defence lines held by other battalions. Markings in green indicate positions which I took on the 12th of July and where I stayed all up to the 16th. On the 16th, we moved and the green arrows show in which direction we moved and what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, at least I'm having some difficulties seeing the green arrows. But before we get to that, do you also have on this map, have you marked the other battalions, where they're located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please just show us, if we just move the map briefly, and you could show us where the other battalions are as you have reflected them on this particular map. Where is the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The 2nd Battalion was positioned from Lomanac Brook, exclusive; then trig point 436, Ladja; then trig point 438, towards the so-called Zuti Most; then trig point 773, Caus; trig point 777, Obadi. And I believe this point here is the road to Rudnik. Up to here was the position of the 2nd Battalion, exclusive of the last point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please show us where the 3rd Battalion would have been.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I was not really familiar with the position of the 3rd Battalion, but I drew my assumptions as to where they were deployed. Across this road, then the lead and zinc mine, three kings, trig point 861; trig point 101.3, quartz; and further on towards trig point 906. But I cannot be quite certain about this because they were far away from me, at least that we see on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, in an earlier order we saw where you had to link up with the 4th Battalion. Where was the 4th Battalion for you to link up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The 4th Battalion was deployed between trig point 555, Ilina Bara, across TT.651 I think in the -- in another map it's called Ornice feature. And they had a kind of semi-circular defence line here pointing towards right for the simple reason that this was an interim area between the Milici and Bratunac Brigades. And this is a stretch as the crow flies of about 2 or 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, looking at this map before we discuss the -- this particular order and the areas which you were ordered to search, could you please point out where your command post would have been. Where was the command post of the 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Are you asking me about the 6th of July or before that date?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, let's start with the 6th of July, because that's the period that we're really interested in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: All right. It was located approximately here in the Magasici or Bozici village sector, close to a house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is there a trig point or something that you can direct our attention to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Well, there is no specific trig point. This is an old map and it doesn't show very clearly that there was a rather good-quality dirt road. And we were billeted in the houses, in the Serbian houses there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, what's the name of the village again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The wider area is called Bozici and some people call it Magasici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what does the map reflect so we have a point of reference?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The map says "Bozici."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you mark it -- could you mark that area perhaps with an "X," so at least later when we're looking at this map we know that the X denotes the forward command post on the 6th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I apologise, but this was not our forward command post; it was our command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you could please show us where it was that you noticed the column. You said that on the night of the 10th and on the day of the 11th, you noticed a column heading in a particular direction. Where would that -- where was that column located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: On the 10th, we noticed smaller groups, at least what we were able to see was not a major column. It was rather groups and smaller columns. And we noticed them in the Jaglici village sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you put a circle around that area so we know that the circle would reflect where the column was when you first saw it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, could you please show us in which direction was this column travelling in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It was travelling, as indicated by this arrow, towards this interim space that existed here much before these events took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So that would be sort of in a north-western --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And from the distance where your men were located, again could you please tell us how many kilometres are we speaking about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: As the crow flies, if you take these points from which they could be observed, I specifically saw them from this point of Vresinje. So let us measure this because we have a scale on the map. Approximately 4 kilometres, as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said "from this point." Which point again are we speaking about? Is that your forward command post as opposed to a command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, could you please put a "Y" at the forward command post so that we know that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It looks more like an "x," but okay. All right. Now, I want to direct your attention back to the order itself. Okay. And this is the order of 14 July 1995, where you're being asked to search the terrain pursuant to an earlier order that was issued by General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in looking at paragraph 1 you indicated that it was rather unclear or there was -- you had some problems with it. First of all, could you please tell us what is paragraph 1 direct -- what area is paragraph 1 directing you to search? Could you show us on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we don't have the translation --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I can't hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First of all, I need you to slow down a little bit and -- so take it from the beginning step by step, slowly. The first part says -- let me read it, you follow along, and then you point to us. It says that: "The 1st Infantry Battalion searched the terrain from the area of the former enclave of Srebrenica on the right side." It says: "The junction of Bratunac/Konjevic Polje." Then it says "Jezestica Road, K316." Now, could you please show us, what is this referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: As I said, it's a rather complicated explanation for one point only. And one might become confused with this. But as it -- as I see it, it could only mean the trig point 316, and I'm pointing at it now. Then the next feature mentioned here is trig point 555 exclusive. Here it is. 555, exclusive. The next feature is Lupoglav, trig point 675, and this is where it is. The next feature is village of Susnjari exclusive. So this is this right-hand or left-hand side --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me stop you. Polako. Slowly. We have to -- now, it says here Bratunac/Konjevic Polje/Zesica road. Where is Konjevic Polje on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I must find it --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I know, but we're going to have to pull it down. Right around --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's the -- that area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where is 316? Without moving the map, please, I think we might be able to handle this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Elevation 316.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- well, let me focus your attention here because I'm a little confused. What does Konjevic Polje have to do with point 316? We looked at this order. It says: "Bratunac/Konjevic Polje/Zesica road 316." What does Konjevic Polje have anything to do with 316?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Only in the sense that somebody wanted to explain that this is a junction of the roads which partly relies on this Bratunac/Konjevic Polje section of the road. And in the next segment it may -- it -- they made it more specific by saying that they were referring to the village of Jezestica, elevation 316.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before we get to the next section, pursuant to this order as you understood it and as you are explaining it to us today, were you being asked to search any part of the terrain from Konjevic Polje, where you pointed out at the top of the map, to 316?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, concretely speaking, where was the starting point of the searching of this terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I would like to say only that this is a border of a whole zone and it's not a starting point when we speak about trig point 316. The starting point was from the positions we had been holding up until the 15th. So from these positions, in fact, we started the search.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now I'm a little confused. Where is 316?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you mark that, please, with a circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, that's behind your line, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would there be any need for you to search behind your line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: There wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why wouldn't there be, just to make sure that we understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Because at the time it would have been nonsensical to leave the existing position to someone else and the area that I have got hold of, and to withdraw backwards, that would be superfluous and totally unreasonable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I think I'm clear on that point now. So getting back, your starting point would have been where, at least pursuant to this particular order, albeit it says 316, where would you have concretely started your searching?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Concretely under this order, I should have started it from 316 up to the Lomanac Brook and the line that travels between the two points.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we could move the map a little bit over. Where -- on this particular day, where are your troops located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: They were located here in this section between trig point 555, Ilina Bara over Vresina, Cizmici, up to Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me stop you. The line that we see right now that exists, that was the -- your defensive zone, was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, at what point -- I believe you did tell us already whether it was the 12th or the 13th, at some point you moved some of your troops. Could you please tell us where you moved them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I moved them only in this section between the Lomanac Brook via Lemesac. There is a feature called Stolice. And up to trig point 532. So approximately three infantry companies were moved. The remaining units, the 1st and the 2nd Infantry Companies remained at their positions for several reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, maybe you can take the marker there and first of all, with an arrow, point in which direction the troops would have moved. And secondly, perhaps with a dotted line, show us where they had actually moved to. So the dotted line would reflect where you moved the troops to, the arrow -- the direction in which they moved.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what day did you leave -- did you move and which day did they arrive at this position.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: We moved to these positions on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So perhaps you could put 12 July there so we know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, concretely speaking, on the 14th of July, 1995, when you received this order, are your troops in the location as we see it now, that is, the 1st and the 2nd and the dotted line which your troops moved to on the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: I would also like to add that on the 12th of July we didn't have this particular section; we failed to link up with the 2nd Battalion. We did that only on the 13th, this shorter section between here and here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So -- all right. So that would be the two last sections that you have, the two last dotted lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, getting back to this particular order, if you could now show us what areas again you're being asked to search. You told us about 316 and how that did not make any sense because you would have to give up territory that you occupied only to re-search it, knowing that there's no enemy behind you. So where is 555? Where is that trig point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Trig point 555 is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And where is trig point 675?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Lupoglav.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And where is the village of Sandici? It says up to the village of Sandici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It's somewhere here on this road. Yes, here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. I've got it -- I have it wrong. It says up to the village of Sandjari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Susnjari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Susnjari, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Susnjari is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then it says -- on the left side. And then it says Lomanac Brook.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then it says: "The village Pale up to the trig point 906." And then it talks about your command post will be in -- where is the command post, according to this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: The command post was in Cizmici, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I could get you to please -- I don't know if we have another colour, but to perhaps draw the line in actuality of what you were asked to search, that is starting with 316, even though in your opinion it doesn't make sense.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Shall I just mark the line or the zone?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, let's start with the line first. Let's keep it simple.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: So this is this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But I'm talking about the entire -- under the order, 316, 555, 687, 906. What is the area, the geographical area, that you're being asked to search?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Then I'll mark the whole area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: This is Susnjari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How far are you supposed to go now, because it looks like a horseshoe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Well, from these starting lines -- in fact, this left flank should stretch some 8 or 9 kilometres. The right flank would be 5 to 6 kilometres long, in roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, in actuality, sir, based on your experience, your knowledge of the terrain, knowing the number of men that you had, was the task that you were being given, the searching of this particular terrain as designated, was it realistic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: No, it wasn't realistic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Aside from the fact that this order was asking you to search terrain that was clear and free, in other words go backwards only to go forwards again --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting to that. It's totally argumentative --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's not argumentative --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it's also misstating the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey doesn't need to whisper. He can stand up and object for Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, we have rules here. Mr. Karnavas, I fail to see your point in asking the witness to mark on those maps, because the witness testified that they had no prisoners, no weapons during this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour. One of the reasons why I'm asking the gentleman to mark it is because, you see, when we see Konjevic Polje it's -- for the Prosecution it's like a bull seeing red and they head for that. And what I'm trying to demonstrate is that this particular order, even though it has Konjevic Polje in it, has nothing to do with Konjevic Polje. And actually I'm showing where the area was that this gentleman, along with his men, were supposed to search. So I do think that it's part of the evidence, as far as where the different battalions were searching, pursuant to orders that we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now we do have Mr. McCloskey on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take it it's going to be procedural, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the description is the Konjevic Polje/Bratunac road. I think after a year we all know what road that is. That's all it says and we're not suggesting there's any great mystery to it. I just wanted to clear that up if it will save time. We know what the Konjevic Polje/Bratunac road is but I think they threw in another village to make it a little clear. That's not really in contest here, that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just have a couple more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And there are other reasons which will become eminently clear in my closing argument, a little bit like a mosaic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if you could -- the area that you're being asked to search, is that realistic, in light of the men that you have at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It's unrealistic, both for the reason of the number of men at my disposal but also because, in fact, I was to go in front of other units. The remaining units would be moving in that direction. And if it were to happen that I was going faster, I may have gone in front of them and friendly fire may have occurred, which in such situations are quite possible. The whole area is huge and it is difficult to negotiate it. So in any case, it was a problem and we did not execute this order in the manner prescribed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just one last question while we're at this subject. If we look at paragraph number 5, there is a completion time of 16 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're given two days to complete this task. Are you saying that even with that amount of time, two full days, you and your men could not accomplish this task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Hardly. Plus there was another force majeure event as far as I remember on the 15th of July. It was raining very hard, which was another restrictive factor in starting this search of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you're being asked to establish your command post at Cizmici. And I apologise for the pronunciation, but I'm a little tired, not that I'm any better when I'm fresh. But when was it that you had established that command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: That command post was set up on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So from that can we conclude that the author of this -- or what can we conclude, seeing that you establish it on the 12th. And now on the 14th you're being asked to establish it? Can you draw any conclusions from that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: We can draw the conclusion that this command post was formalised in this format.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But what about the author? Here you're being asked on the 14th to establish something that's already been established, are you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now -- and just for the record, could you kind of mark that somehow so we know -- with an "A" for instance so we know that this is the command post, the area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, before we leave this particular document, I want you to look at it for a second. Does it state in this document to whom it was distributed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105
utterances.text: It says that it was delivered to the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And before we go on, I believe we're through with the map. And we want to thank the -- Mr. Usher for assisting us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, unrelated to the specific testimony, but just a matter of a fair amount of importance, it is really unclear from the Prosecution what the relevancy of that was, as the Court requested from counsel. Counsel has stated he's going to do his mosaic in his closing argument. That's really -- under this system doesn't work, because we need to know what we're cross-examining about. And in some systems like this, the Prosecution has rebuttal to the closing argument, which because we have the burden of proof, it's normal. And I will be asking, if we can't tie this material up or at least have some showing of relevancy, I'm going to need to be able to have a short rebuttal argument, otherwise Mr. Karnavas in his mosaic is going to reveal all and the Prosecution will have nothing to say about it. And before Mr. Karnavas reveals all at the end, I would like to have a response. And I don't know if we need to get into this at this late date, especially the relevance, in front of the witness. But perhaps in the morning we might get an idea of the mosaic to come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, do you want to tell us something now, or we may wait until tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe in delayed gratification. I'll give it -- I'll respond right now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the problem is is the witness is hearing the relevance and the witness is going to be talking about these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I didn't jump up, Your Honour. I didn't jump up and make this objection. We can excuse the witness for the evening --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- and I can make my little five-minute presentation. I don't have a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to give your evidence. I'm afraid you have to stay here overnight and during your stay in The Hague you are still under oath. So don't let anybody talk to you and don't talk to anybody about your testimony. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's have your closing argument for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, thank you, Mr. President. I always like to argue as much as I can, and as early as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: (Redacted) He did draw a map for the Office of the Prosecution where he outlined exactly where his folks were throughout those critical days. The searching of the terrain has been a somewhat contentious or an issue that has been litigated somewhat in this particular case. And that -- also in addition to that, we -- lots of documents have come in either through Mr. Butler or other witnesses, and a significant amount of importance has been placed on the content of the document as if the documents are accurate, or purport to be accurate. So what I'm trying to demonstrate here is that first of all, whoever wrote this document - and tomorrow we'll see that it doesn't have the authentication that it would necessarily have, because it doesn't show to whom it was distributed and what have you, but rather says the chief of staff and who we all know and will learn again tomorrow was not there - but we see there is information being put on official documents or what would appear to be official documents that are not correct. And through this little exercise I'm trying to demonstrate several things. One is the danger of circumstantial evidence. Because circumstantially when we look at this, we can say, well, yes they could easily have accomplished this task. Number two, the Konjevic Polje thing, and I was rather light about it, but it does draw one's attention. So this could give the wrong impression that in reading this when we say "junction of Bratunac/Konjevic Polje," one might think that this particular battalion was also responsible for searching the terrain. And we know that at least in that area there was some activity by MUP that had nothing to do with the Bratunac Brigade. And so that's the other point that I'm trying to demonstrate. And as I indicated, through this gentleman I'm trying to show that, one, this order has some information that's not accurate, such as to establish a command post that's already been established, to search terrain which has already -- has always been clear because their line was ahead of them. And I'm trying to show that perhaps when it comes time to evaluate all of this evidence, we have to be very careful not to place too much emphasis on what's written, because it may lead us down to the wrong path. And this was a perfect opportunity, because the next document -- you see, I have some more. They are all here, neatly piled up. I'm going to go through one of the other maps, that famous map that says "Colonel Zivanovic, zone of responsibility." We're going to have an opportunity to look at that map again. Because of the title, we may think that this is an official map that has some importance. Because it has "zone of responsibility," it has been given a certain amount of prominence by Mr. Butler --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we understand the relevance of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He asked me a question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We're not on to that topic yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, he asked me a question and he shouldn't ask me questions if he doesn't want the full answer. I'm going to use this again as a vehicle to get to that one to show that documents are misleading, so when they pull out some logbook and say oh, so-and-so was here, before we make that assumption that that was in fact -- a fact, we should have perhaps other witnesses to corroborate it. That's all. So it's -- there are no tricks, there are no tricks, just good old-fashioned lawyering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think it's time for the break. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do I get my three-minute's response, Your Honour? I thought that was a lot more than why it was relevant. I don't feel a need to, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is it necessary? Maybe we could have it tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't need to say anything, Your Honour, but I appreciate that he's saying it's to show credibility of documents. And that's what I was asking. All the rest of the speech wasn't really necessary, but I think I don't need to rebut that. I think we understand what's going on.
